name: To
catalog_citation: Noss, Philip A. 1977. Compounding in To: the dynamics of a closed pidgin. Studies in African Linguistics, Supplement 7 (December 1977), pp. 185-196. Full-issue PDF, journals.flvc.org/sal/article/download/107646/102959.
catalog_quote: While its lexical base is not Gbaya, and is indeed of the other branch of the Adamawa-Eastern phylum from Gbaya, To possesses no phones that do not occur in the Gbaya inventory. The functional load of tone is also severely limited with no minimal pairs in evidence, a marked difference from both Gbaya and Mbum, where tone plays a relatively important role. Its grammar is likewise restricted, with a minimum of affixes and relational items. ... [fn.4, p.188:] I prefer to call them compounds because they are not mere circumlocutions, but clearly defined structures. Evidence of this is the internal tone shifting that occurs in the same patterns as is found in Gbaya compounds.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both parts of the deciding quotation are verbatim in the held full-issue PDF/text at the stated places (p.186 sec. 4; fn.4 at foot of p.188), and the 'no stress/accent mention' claim in prule is reproducible by grep over pp.185-196. (2) Deciding source: a 1977 specific-feature article by the language's principal modern fieldworker; thin on phonology by nature, but Glottolog lists it as the sole descriptive reference (n_glottolog_desc_refs=1), and reference/author/title searches on Glottolog plus archive.org turned up no phonology, grammar or later study of To — only Tessmann 1931 (comparative overview/wordlist) and works on the distinct Labi initiation language. The language is extinct (AES: extinct; last fluent consultant died 1976), so no better description will appear. (3) The coding 'tonal, no stress rule stated, domain UNSTATED' matches what Noss says: tone is prese
